refnamediv.refpurpose: Inspect the platform-authentication state and produce attestation

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: trustctl inspects the platform-authentication state maintained by platformd-trustd.service8, evaluates its policies, and produces attestation. It is a client of the io.platformd.Trust varlink7 interface; the reading commands require no privilege, while the attestation commands (attest, attest-token, enroll, activate-credential) must run as root. The daemon restricts evidence production because it is a signing operation on the shared TPM. provision and remove-boot-reference require privilege to update boot references. verify-endorsement, verify-attestation, and appraise-attestation process supplied evidence offline and require neither privilege, a running daemon, nor a TPM.

listitem.para: Show the boot evidence and a summary of the platform-authentication state.
List the tracked login sessions with their lock and verification state.
Show the record for the session ID, including the identity behind it and whether that identity is verified.

Evaluate POLICY for the session ID and print the result, stable reason code, descriptive reason, and freshness window. The policies are verified-boot, fresh-user-verification, and local-trusted-session. The result is policy-satisfied or denied.
Show the recorded authentication events, most recent first, and whether each event established verification freshness.
Show the measured-boot PCRs of the SHA-256 bank and the boot grade.

Show the runtime authentication measurement log: the authentication, lock, and sleep state events folded into the extend-only TPM NV index, with the baseline and current values needed to replay it. Version 2 extends the SHA-256 digest of each serialized record. Its boot ID, timestamps, provenance, and payload are included in that digest.

Produce a TPM quote over the boot PCRs, bound to NONCE (a hexadecimal string). If none is given a random nonce is generated. The quote is verifiable against the attestation key's public part without trusting the service.

Produce a platformd-specific JSON evidence envelope containing the TPM quote, boot measurements, and runtime log. Only the embedded TPM structures are signed; local assertions are unsigned. The envelope is not an IETF Entity Attestation Token.

Verify a version 2 platformd attestation envelope against an independently supplied Attestation Key and challenge. The key file contains the hexadecimal marshaled TPM2B_PUBLIC, with optional surrounding whitespace. Both inputs must be regular files; the envelope is limited to 16 MiB and the key file to 4096 bytes. The challenge is required and must contain 1 through 64 bytes encoded as hexadecimal.

Verify the quote and NV certification signatures, challenge, signer and TPM lifecycle, quoted PCR digest, NV definition and value, and exact runtime-log replay. Print the successful checks and retained event count as JSON. No result is printed when verification fails.

Success establishes evidence integrity under the supplied key. It does not establish key enrollment, approved boot state, complete boot history, trusted timestamps, authentication freshness, or access authorization. Local assertions remain unsigned. An empty retained runtime log is valid only when its baseline equals the certified value; it contains no authentication evidence. The requester must generate, expire, and consume its challenges. Reusing a challenge is not detected by this command.

Verify an attestation envelope as described for verify-attestation, then compare its SHA-256 PCR 11 value against an independently approved reference for the specified phase. All options are required. No local reference directory is consulted.

The reference is a regular JSON file limited to 1 MiB, in the format produced by systemd-measure calculate --bank=sha256 --phase=STRING --json=short. The root object contains only sha256, an array of 1 through 1024 objects. Each object contains exactly phase, pcr, and hash: a nonempty phase string of at most 1024 bytes without ASCII control characters, the integer 11, and a 32-byte digest encoded as hexadecimal. Duplicate keys and unsupported banks or PCRs are rejected. Every candidate is validated. At least one candidate must match both the requested phase and the verified PCR value.

Print the verification checks, retained event count, approvedPcr11Matched, and approvedPhase as JSON on success. No result is printed on failure. Approval applies only to PCR 11 for the selected phase. It does not establish approved firmware, Secure Boot policy, the complete running system, key enrollment, or authentication freshness. The caller selects the key, reference, and phase independently of the submitted token, and owns challenge expiry and single-use enforcement.

Verify the Endorsement Key certificate in the exact JSON object returned by GetEnrollment. The certificate public key must match the submitted Endorsement Key. Only the platformd ECC P-256 storage-key template is supported. The evidence must be a regular file of at most 64 KiB.

The trust anchor is an explicitly selected, self-signed root certificate in a regular PEM file of at most 64 KiB. The optional certificate-chain file contains at most 16 untrusted intermediate certificates in PEM format and is limited to 1 MiB. Each DER certificate is limited to 16 KiB. No system trust store or network retrieval is used.

The required revocations file is a regular JSON file limited to 1 MiB. Its root object contains only crls, an array of 1 through 32 objects. Each object contains exactly distributionPoint, a URI from a certificate's CRL distribution points, and pem, one PEM-encoded X.509 CRL. Distribution points must use full HTTP or HTTPS URIs, matched exactly. The URI selects supplied revocation material; it is not fetched. A current, matching CRL is required for every non-root certificate. Certificate and CRL signatures, scope, validity periods, and revocation status are checked using the verifier's current wall clock.

Indirect CRLs are supported only when their signer is on the validated certificate chain. Separate CRL-signer paths, relative distribution-point names, reason-partitioned CRLs, and delta CRLs are not supported. CRL signatures must use SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512; RSA-PSS CRL signatures are not supported. Certificate paths are checked at OpenSSL authentication security level 2.

Print an io.platformd.Trust.EndorsementVerification.v1 report as JSON on success. No result is printed on failure. Success establishes certificate validity under the selected root and a matching Endorsement Key. It does not prove possession of that key, bind an Attestation Key, identify an account, approve boot state, or establish authentication. The caller owns anchor selection and revocation-data maintenance.

Create a credential-activation challenge for the exact JSON object returned by GetEnrollment, supplied as a regular file of at most 64 KiB. In explicit-key mode, the independently provisioned endorsement-key file contains a hexadecimal marshaled TPM2B_PUBLIC and is limited to 4096 bytes. The evidence is not a trust anchor. This command supports the platformd ECC P-256 key templates and requires tpm2_makecredential. It does not access a local TPM.

Alternatively, supply the certificate-verification options described for verify-endorsement. The same parsed evidence is verified before creating enrollment state or invoking tpm2_makecredential. The verified Endorsement Key becomes the enrollment pin. Mixing certificate options with --endorsement-key= is rejected. A previously printed verification report is not accepted as authority.

The state directory must already exist, be absolute, owned by the effective user, and have mode 0700. Symlink path components are rejected. State files have mode 0600. No default directory, device identity, certificate authority, or account association is selected. The lifetime must be 1 through 600 seconds. Expiry uses the verifier's suspend-aware clock and boot ID. Only a hash of the expected response is retained.

Print the key identifier, request identifier, credential, and encrypted secret as JSON. The key identifier is SHA-256 of the complete marshaled Attestation Key public area. An active, revoked, or unexpired pending enrollment cannot be replaced. An inactive enrollment retains its original key pins. Certificate mode also includes an endorsementVerification report in the initial challenge output. The enrollment retains key pins, not a continuously checked certificate status. Later certificate expiry or revocation does not automatically revoke an active enrollment.

Complete the matching credential-activation challenge. The response file contains 32 hexadecimal-encoded bytes recovered by the attester. It must be a regular file owned by the effective user, with mode 0600, one hard link, and no final symlink. Never place the response in a command argument or environment variable.
An unreadable or unsafe response file is rejected before the response is submitted to the enrollment store.

A matching attempt consumes the pending challenge, including an incorrect response, expiry, or a verifier reboot. A different request identifier does not consume the current challenge. Success activates the enrollment under the selected endorsement-key pin. Credential activation itself does not validate a certificate; certificate-mode validation occurs when enrollment-begin runs.

Inspect or revoke an enrollment. Revocation is durable and removes pending authentication requests. Revoked keys cannot be reactivated. A replacement Attestation Key requires a separate enrollment; no device or account relationship is inferred. Concurrent access that conflicts with a held state lock fails with EBUSY.

Create one expiring authentication request for an active enrollment. The regular JSON input file, limited to 4096 bytes, contains exactly uid, sessionId, audience, and operationDigestHex. The UID is an integer less than 4294967295. Session and audience are nonempty printable ASCII strings of at most 256 bytes. The operation digest is 32 bytes in lowercase hexadecimal. Its input encoding and account mapping are defined by the application, not by trustd.

Print a request containing a random 32-byte challenge. Pass its nested request.context object to verifyctl verify-context on the attester, then obtain an attestation token with the same challenge. The lifetime is 1 through 600 seconds, measured by the verifier. An unexpired pending request cannot be overwritten.

Consume a matching unexpired request and appraise its evidence under the active enrollment. Consumption is durable before appraisal; malformed evidence, an unapproved reference, or a missing authentication declaration cannot be retried with the same request. A verifier reboot, expiry, or revocation invalidates the request. The verifier checks expiry again after appraisal and report formatting, before writing a successful result. Expiry during processing consumes the request without returning a result.

Require valid TPM evidence, the request challenge in both TPM structures, approved PCR 11 for the selected phase, and an exact measured SubmitVerificationEvent declaration for the requested UID, session, audience, and operation digest. A later retained lock invalidation for that session, or any sleep invalidation, rejects the declaration. Missing or unmeasured declarations fail closed. The explicit policy option accepts the privileged host's declaration of PAM completion. It does not prove a particular factor, user consent, application identity, or the integrity of the privileged host.

Print a successful appraisal as JSON. Expiry and single use are enforced by the verifier's state, not by device timestamps. The result is a snapshot; the application must bind it to its authenticated connection, account, and pending operation before granting access. These commands provide no network listener or transport authentication.
Show the enrollment evidence: the Endorsement Key public key and, when present, its manufacturer certificate, together with the Attestation Key public key and TPM name.

Complete a credential-activation challenge, given the credential blob and encrypted secret produced by a verifier's TPM2_MakeCredential (both hexadecimal). The challenge is recovered only if the attestation key and the Endorsement Key are resident together. The verifier must independently establish trust in the Endorsement Key; credential activation alone does not establish manufacturer provenance.

Compute the expected boot measurement from the sections of the unified kernel image UKI, using systemd-measure1, and record it for one boot entry. REFERENCE-ID defaults to the UKI filename. This is normally run by the kernel-install8 plugin on each kernel installation.
The installed measurement tool must support each measured section present in the UKI. Images containing .efifw require support for --efifw=. If calculation fails, no new reference is written.
Remove the reference for one boot entry. The kernel-install8 plugin uses this when removing a kernel.
Print a short help text and exit.

refsect1.title: Exit status
refsect1.para: On success 0 is returned, a non-zero failure code otherwise.

listitem.para: The directory holding the io.platformd.Trust socket. Defaults to /run/platformd-trustd.
